links.targetTitle: Aligned Delegate recognition proves control of two Ethereum

title: Signer onboarding binds a key to an accountable identifier through a signed intent message
content:
A.2.11.1.3.2.1.2.1.1 requires a cryptographically signed message "demonstrating control of the signer address intended for Multisig participation," containing four elements: a statement of intent to join the specified multisig, the multisig address, the signer address, and "the signer's handle, entity name, or other identifying affiliation sufficient to establish accountability." It is shared with the Multisig Administrator (A.2.11.1.3.2.1.2.1.2).

Each element defends against a specific failure. Proof of control prevents adding an address whose key nobody holds — an unnoticed way to silently raise the effective threshold, or to permanently strand a multisig. Naming the multisig prevents a signature gathered for one purpose being replayed to enroll the address elsewhere. Stating intent prevents an address being enrolled by someone else on the holder's behalf.

The accountability element is the notable design choice. It accepts "handle" or "entity name" — a pseudonym is sufficient, provided it is a persistent identity that can be held responsible. This matches the Atlas's broader stance of protecting participant pseudonymity while still requiring attributable action, and contrasts sharply with the Named-identity plus KYC demanded of external whitehats under Safe Harbor.

The pattern generalizes: what security actually requires is not knowing who someone legally is, but that a durable identity is attached to the key and will bear the consequences of its use.
description: Before joining, a signer signs a message naming the multisig, the signer address, an explicit intent to join, and a handle or entity affiliation sufficient to establish accountability
